source.title: Network packet
source.source_scope: Terminology, architecture, framing, packet contents, Internet protocol, NASA Deep Space Network, MPEG packetized stream, NICAM, references and related concepts as supplied.

design_principles: Network packet is modeled as a first-class dynamic data object.
Packet components, fields, lifecycle operations, protocol layers, and examples are separate nodes.
Relationships encode mechanisms and direction rather than generic relatedness.
Strict OSI terminology is preserved separately from broader networking usage.
Examples are connected to the general packet model without replacing the source's framing.

nodes.label: Network packet
nodes.description: A formatted unit of data carried by a packet-switched network; composed of control information and user data/payload.

nodes.label: Packet switching
nodes.description: A networking method in which transmission-medium bandwidth is shared among multiple communication sessions.

nodes.label: Circuit switching
nodes.description: A networking method in which circuits are preallocated for a session and data is typically sent as a continuous bit stream.

nodes.label: Control information
nodes.description: Information used to deliver, validate, classify, sequence, prioritize, or otherwise process packet payload.

nodes.label: Payload
nodes.description: User data carried on behalf of an application.

nodes.label: Header
nodes.description: Control-information region conventionally placed at the beginning of a packet.

nodes.label: Trailer
nodes.description: Control-information region conventionally placed at the end of a packet.

nodes.label: Packet format
nodes.description: The protocol-defined organization and representation of packet fields.

nodes.label: Protocol data unit (PDU)
nodes.description: A layer-specific data unit; the source distinguishes packet strictly as a Layer 3 PDU.

nodes.label: OSI Layer 2 / Data Link
nodes.description: Data-link layer where the source terminology uses frame for the PDU.

nodes.label: OSI Layer 3 / Network
nodes.description: Network layer where packet strictly denotes the PDU.

nodes.label: OSI Layer 4 / Transport
nodes.description: Transport layer where TCP data is called a segment and UDP-style data a datagram.

nodes.label: Frame
nodes.description: Data-link layer data unit.

nodes.label: Segment
nodes.description: Transport-layer data unit associated here with TCP.

nodes.label: Datagram
nodes.description: Transport-layer data unit associated here with datagram-oriented transport.

nodes.label: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
nodes.description: Reliable transport protocol commonly layered above IP packet service.

nodes.label: Internet Protocol (IP)
nodes.description: Packet-based network protocol whose packets contain header and payload and provide best-effort delivery.

nodes.label: Ethernet
nodes.description: Link technology whose frames carry IP packets as payload.

nodes.label: TCP/IP
nodes.description: Protocol architecture used as the source's principal example of layered packet communication.

nodes.label: End-to-end principle
nodes.description: Network-layer service does not itself guarantee delivery, non-duplication, or ordering; reliable transport may provide these properties.

nodes.label: Postal-letter analogy
nodes.description: Packet header is compared with an envelope, payload with its contents, and footer/trailer with a signature at the bottom.

nodes.label: Error detection
nodes.description: Detection of transmission or packet errors.

nodes.label: Error correction
nodes.description: Correction of detected errors where the protocol and circumstances permit it.

nodes.label: Multiple-host addressing
nodes.description: Ability to identify sending and receiving hosts through network addresses.

nodes.label: Source network address
nodes.description: Network address identifying the sending host.

nodes.label: Destination network address
nodes.description: Network address identifying the receiving host.

nodes.label: Checksum
nodes.description: Computed value used to detect discrepancies between transmitted and received data.

nodes.label: Parity bits
nodes.description: Error-detection bits that may be included in packet-related formats.

nodes.label: Cyclic redundancy check (CRC)
nodes.description: Error-detection code that may be carried by a packet or its enclosing data-link frame.

nodes.label: Sequencing information
nodes.description: Control information used to represent ordering/sequence.

nodes.label: Transmitter calculation
nodes.description: Checksum or similar error-control value calculated before transmission.

nodes.label: Receiver recalculation
nodes.description: Receiver recomputes an error-control value and compares it with the transmitted value.

nodes.label: Packet correction
nodes.description: Possible correction of a packet when discrepancies are detected and the protocol supports correction.

nodes.label: Packet discard
nodes.description: Dropping a packet when it cannot or should not be accepted/corrected.

nodes.label: Packet loss
nodes.description: Loss resulting from packet discard or other network behavior.

nodes.label: Protocol recovery
nodes.description: Protocol mechanisms that deal with packet loss, including reliable transport behavior.

nodes.label: Time to live (TTL)
nodes.description: A field decreased by one at each network hop to bound packet circulation.

nodes.label: Hop limit
nodes.description: Hop-count mechanism analogous to TTL for limiting packet lifetime.

nodes.label: Network hop
nodes.description: A forwarding step through a network node/router.

nodes.label: Routing loop
nodes.description: Closed forwarding circuit through which packets may circulate.

nodes.label: Network congestion
nodes.description: Condition where offered traffic overwhelms available forwarding/transmission capacity.

nodes.label: Broadcast storm
nodes.description: Severe network traffic condition associated in the source with switching loops and Ethernet's lack of TTL.

nodes.label: Ethernet lacks TTL
nodes.description: Ethernet packets have no TTL field according to the source.

nodes.label: Packet length
nodes.description: Field that may specify overall packet length; in some networks length is implied by transmission duration.

nodes.label: Protocol identifier
nodes.description: Field identifying the protocol carried so the protocol stack can process multiple packet types.

nodes.label: Packet priority
nodes.description: Field used by some networks to select a priority queue.

nodes.label: Quality of service (QoS)
nodes.description: Mechanism for differentiating treatment of traffic, including prioritization under congestion.

nodes.label: Packet queue
nodes.description: Queue from which packets are processed; higher-priority queues may be serviced faster under congestion.

nodes.label: Variable-length payload
nodes.description: Payload is generally variable length up to protocol/equipment limits.

nodes.label: Maximum packet/payload size
nodes.description: Upper size limit imposed by a network protocol and sometimes equipment along the route.

nodes.label: Packet fragmentation
nodes.description: Breaking a larger packet into smaller packets when required by the network.

nodes.label: Packet reassembly
nodes.description: Combining fragmented packet pieces back into the original logical data unit.

nodes.label: Packet routing
nodes.description: Forwarding packets toward their destination based on addressing and network topology.

nodes.label: Network addressing
nodes.description: Use of source and destination addresses to support packet routing.

nodes.label: Framing
nodes.description: Protocol conventions for distinguishing and formatting packet elements.

nodes.label: Byte-level delimiting
nodes.description: Formatting based on 8-bit bytes and special delimiter characters, as described for PPP.

nodes.label: Location-based framing
nodes.description: Protocol convention where header/data boundaries are established by location relative to packet start.

nodes.label: Bit-level formatting
nodes.description: Formatting protocol information at bit rather than byte granularity.

nodes.label: Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP)
nodes.description: Example protocol that formats packets in 8-bit bytes and uses special characters to delimit elements.

nodes.label: IP packet
nodes.description: IP packet consisting of header and payload, with fixed and optional header fields.

nodes.label: IP header
nodes.description: Header of an IP packet containing fixed and optional fields.

nodes.label: IP payload
nodes.description: Data immediately following an IP header; no IP trailer.

nodes.label: IP has no trailer

nodes.label: Ethernet frame

nodes.label: Ethernet header

nodes.label: Ethernet trailer
nodes.description: Ethernet frame trailer.

nodes.label: TCP segment
nodes.description: Transport-layer TCP segment carried by IP.

nodes.label: TCP reliability
nodes.description: TCP can provide delivery protection, duplicate suppression, and in-order delivery over IP's best-effort packet service.

nodes.label: TCP retransmission
nodes.description: Reliable transport response to lost packets/segments.

nodes.label: Delivery guarantee
nodes.description: Guarantee of delivery; not provided by IP itself per the source.

nodes.label: Non-duplication
nodes.description: Guarantee that data is not duplicated; not provided by IP itself per the source.

nodes.label: In-order delivery

nodes.label: Packet definition
nodes.description: A network packet is a formatted unit of data carried by a packet-switched network; it contains control information and payload.

nodes.label: Control information
nodes.description: Control information supports delivery and is typically located in headers and trailers.

nodes.label: Switching distinction
nodes.description: Packet switching shares transmission-medium bandwidth while circuit switching preallocates circuits.

nodes.label: OSI terminology
nodes.description: Strictly in the seven-layer OSI model, packet is Layer 3; Layer 2 uses frame and Layer 4 uses segment/datagram.

nodes.label: Addressing
nodes.description: Source and destination network addresses support packet routing.

nodes.label: Error handling
nodes.description: Packets may contain checksums, parity bits, or CRCs; mismatches may lead to correction or discard.

nodes.label: TTL
nodes.description: TTL decreases at each network hop and reaching zero causes discard.

nodes.label: Other fields
nodes.description: Packets may contain length, protocol identifier, priority, and variable-length payload fields.
nodes.source_section: Contents > Length / Protocol identifier / Priority / Payload

nodes.label: Framing
nodes.description: Protocols use byte delimiters, positional conventions, or bit-level formatting to distinguish packet elements.

nodes.label: IP/TCP/Ethernet
nodes.description: TCP segments can be carried in IP packets, which can be carried in Ethernet frames.

nodes.label: IP service
nodes.description: IP does not guarantee delivery, non-duplication, or in-order delivery.

nodes.label: Examples
nodes.description: CCSDS, MPEG PES, and NICAM illustrate packetization in spacecraft telemetry, media transport, and digital audio.

nodes.label: NICAM
nodes.description: NICAM scrambles packet data with a nine-bit pseudo-random generator to reduce adjacent-channel signal patterning.

relationships.mechanism: Packets are the formatted data units carried by packet-switched networks.
Packet switching shares bandwidth among sessions; circuit switching preallocates circuits.
Control information supports delivery and processing.
Payload is user/application data carried by the packet.
Control information is typically placed in headers.
Control information may also be placed in trailers.
Packet structure can support error detection.
Source/destination addressing enables delivery among multiple hosts.
A packet is formatted according to protocol conventions.
Packet is a layer-specific PDU in the strict Layer 3 terminology.
In OSI terminology packet strictly refers to a Layer 3 PDU.
TTL decreases by one at each network hop.
A decreasing TTL prevents indefinite circulation.
Closed packet circuits can cause packet buildup and congestion.
Packet is discarded when TTL reaches zero.
Without a TTL field, switching loops can produce broadcast storms.
Detection can precede correction where supported.
